heading: Transfer of excess or surplus educationally useful equipment to public schools

tree.heading: Authorization
tree.text: The Sergeant at Arms and Doorkeeper of the Senate may directly, or through the General Services Administration, transfer title to excess or surplus educationally useful equipment to a public school. Any such transfer shall be completed at the lowest possible cost to the public school and the Senate.

tree.heading: Regulations
tree.text: The Committee on Rules and Administration of the Senate shall prescribe regulations to carry out the provisions of this section.

tree.heading: Deposit of receipts
tree.text: Receipts from reimbursements for the costs of transfer of excess or surplus educationally useful equipment under this section,1 shall be deposited in the United States Treasury for credit to the account for the “Sergeant at Arms and Doorkeeper of the Senate” within the contingent fund of the Senate.

tree.heading: Definitions
tree.text: For the purposes of this section:

children.text: The term “public school” means a 2 elementary school or secondary school, as such terms are defined in section 7801 of title 20.

The term “educationally useful equipment” means computers and related peripheral tools, including printers, modems, routers, servers, computer keyboards, scanners, and other telecommunications and research equipment, that are appropriate for use in public school education.

tree.heading: Effective date
tree.text: This section shall take effect beginning with fiscal year 1997 and shall be effective each fiscal year thereafter.

notes.heading: Codification
notes.text: Section was formerly classified to section 117b–2 of this title prior to editorial reclassification and renumbering as this section. Section is from the Congressional Operations Appropriations Act, 1997, which is title I of the Legislative Branch Appropriations Act, 1997.

notes.heading: Amendments
notes.text: 2015—Subsec. (d)(1). Pub. L. 114–95 substituted “elementary school or secondary school, as such terms are defined in section 7801” for “public elementary or secondary school as such terms are defined in section 7801”. 2002—Subsec. (d)(1). Pub. L. 107–110 substituted “7801” for “8801”.

notes.heading: Effective Date of 2015 Amendment
notes.text: Amendment by Pub. L. 114–95 effective Dec. 10, 2015, except with respect to certain noncompetitive programs and competitive programs, see section 5 of Pub. L. 114–95, set out as a note under section 6301 of Title 20, Education.

notes.heading: Effective Date of 2002 Amendment
notes.text: Amendment by Pub. L. 107–110 effective Jan. 8, 2002, except with respect to certain noncompetitive programs and competitive programs, see section 5 of Pub. L. 107–110, set out as an Effective Date note under section 6301 of Title 20, Education.
